decision.required_timing_wording: At 3.0 ns, the logic-only M416 selected slice passes PrimeTime pre-layout data-path setup/hold timing with an ideal clock, ZeroWireload and no SPEF: worst setup slack is +0.759794 ns at the slow library and worst hold slack is +0.017835 ns using the fast min library. Setup, hold, out_setup and out_hold are 100% met. Recovery/removal and part of min-pulse coverage are explicitly not signed off.
decision.required_formality_wording: M421 established unconstrained-primary-input sequential observational equivalence over 1,268 ports and 4,100 observable DFF compare points. The 320 unobservable debug-counter DFFs are not internal-state equivalence points. Do not claim all internal state equivalence.

all_checks.interpretation: The four data-path timing categories are fully covered. The aggregate is not full timing-check signoff.

findings.title: M422's Error/Fatal shell guard is not fail-closed under Bash set -e
findings.detail: The runner writes `! grep -Eq '^(Error|Fatal):' pt.raw.log`. Commands in a negated-list context are exempt from Bash errexit, so a matching tool error does not terminate the script. The sealed M422 raw log contains zero Error/Fatal lines and the independent run is clean, therefore the current numeric conclusion survives; however this guard cannot be cited as proof that arbitrary future logs are rejected.
findings.repair_gate: Use an explicit `if grep -Eq ...; then exit; fi` gate in every new PT/PTPX runner. M424's independent runner already uses this repaired form.

findings.title: coverage_gate_pass is narrower than aggregate PrimeTime timing-check coverage
findings.detail: M422 correctly records 100% met for setup, hold, out_setup and out_hold, but its receipt-level name coverage_gate_pass can be read too broadly. Aggregate coverage is 27,136/51,736 met (52%), with 4,100 recovery, 4,100 removal and 16,400 conditional min-pulse checks untested. The no_startpoint_clock count belongs to reset recovery/removal; no_clock belongs to asynchronous CDN pulse-width conditions, not to the core data-path clock.
findings.repair_gate: Use `data_path_setup_hold_coverage_pass` in paper-facing tables and state the three untested classes explicitly. Do not say all timing checks are covered or that recovery/removal is signed off.

findings.title: Both PT runs retain two SDC-version warnings
findings.detail: PrimeTime emits the same two warnings that SDC version 2.1 does not match the requested version. Link, constraint application, critical paths, slacks and coverage reproduce exactly, so this is not a numeric blocker.
findings.repair_gate: Normalize the SDC version declaration in the next regenerated mapped SDC or document the warning count; do not silently suppress unrelated PT warnings.
